model_description: A tiny per-triple scorer. It builds a mask from row 4 of the [B,5,1024] input and computes six closed-form dependence statistics between receptor R (row 1) and neighbour-ligand signal L (row 0) over real contact cells only. The statistics are Spearman, Pearson, rank partial correlation (ranks of R and L residualised on rows 2-3), OLS slope of R on L, a high-vs-low ligand tercile contrast of R, and a neighbour-count split contrast. A small masked DeepSets branch is run in parallel. Its per-cell inputs are within-triple centred ranks of L and R and their product, and it applies a shared 2-layer phi, masks, then mean+max pools. The statistics and the pooled embedding are concatenated and passed to a 2-layer MLP head. The head emits one sigmoid-bounded score per triple, shape [B,1]. Rows 2-3 are used only as nuisance covariates (regressed out, or used as a split key) and are never fed to the network as direct evidence. All statistics are computed under no_grad with the mask applied first. They are zeroed when a triple has too few contacts.
mathematical_definition:
Input x in R^{B x 5 x N}. Let m = x[:,4,:] in {0,1}, n = sum_j m_j, L = x[:,0,:], R = x[:,1,:], Z = x[:,2:4,:], valid = 1[n >= min_contacts].
Masked average ranks: rank_i(v) = sum_j m_j 1[v_j < v_i] + 0.5 (sum_j m_j 1[v_j = v_i] + 1), computed by pairwise comparison over valid columns only; rank is set to 0 at padded columns. Centre and scale to unit masked variance to get rL, rR.
Stats (all masked sums divided by n, eps-guarded):
 s1 = Spearman = masked Pearson(rL, rR).
 s2 = masked Pearson(L, R).
 s3 = rank partial correlation: regress rL and rR (separately) on design D=[1, masked-standardised Z1, Z2] with ridge-regularised normal equations (3x3 solve with lambda I); s3 = masked Pearson of the two residual vectors.
 s4 = OLS slope of R on L = masked cov(L,R) / (masked var(L)+eps), then asinh.
 s5 = tercile contrast = (mean R over cells with rank(L) in the top third - mean R over bottom third) / pooled masked std(R), then asinh.
 s6 = count-split contrast = Spearman(rL,rR) within cells whose row 3 is above the masked median minus the same within cells at or below it (row 3 is only a split key); guarded to 0 if either half has fewer than min_contacts/2 cells.
stats = valid * [s1..s6] in R^6, no gradient.
DeepSets: per-cell u_j = [rL_j, rR_j, rL_j*rR_j]; h_j = W2 relu(W1 u_j); mean-pool = sum_j m_j h_j / max(n,1); max-pool = max_j over (h_j masked to -1e4 at padded columns), set to 0 if n=0; e = concat(mean-pool, max-pool) in R^{2*embed_dim}.
Head: z = concat(stats, e); y = W4 dropout(relu(W3 z)); score = sigmoid(y) in [0,1], output [B,1]. Because of the regressor output contract, the score is trained against the 0/1 target. Permutation invariance holds because ranks, sums, means, max and quantile splits are all order-free.
motivation: proposed_change: reproduce the human-cited lr_contact_contrast_gbm_head design, i.e. build an explicit non-padded contact-cell mask, compute closed-form masked statistics (Spearman, Pearson, rank partial correlation with rows 2-3 as nuisance, OLS slope, tercile contrast, neighbour-count split), concatenate them with a small masked DeepSets embedding, and fuse them with a 2-layer MLP head. causal_hypothesis: receptor-only and non-spatial scores sit at random level and the Spearman baseline is confounded because every non-injected R x sender x receiver pair gets an equal-sized perturbation from an unobserved ligand. Multiple masked closed-form dependence statistics, with rank partial correlation removing the rows 2-3 nuisance covariates and tercile/count contrasts, give a complementary low-variance evidence vector, and a small MLP fuses them without overfitting 60 datasets. Closed-form statistics carry the inductive bias that the coupling is a dependence of R on neighbour L rather than a mean difference. The tiny head keeps variance low across tiles. The output is a bounded score [B,1] to meet the run's regressor output contract.

focus_areas: Choose epochs, lr and dropout on a tile-grouped split of TRAIN only. Use validation only for the final comparison.
Numerical guards in the masked statistics (ties, tiny n, near-singular partialling design), since NaN or inf features would be the main failure.
Ablate one thing at a time: drop DeepSets, then drop the partial-correlation feature, then drop the tercile contrast.
Hold the parameter count and the feature set fixed if hidden width is varied.
constraints: VRAM: stay well under the 6.37 GB effective cap (target <= 5 GB). The dominant memory is the pairwise rank comparison, about 4 MB per triple per [N x N] float tensor, so batch_size 32 uses well under 1 GB. Raise batch_size only while measured peak stays below the target.
Do not increase parameter count (human directive). The baseline is about 1.7k parameters.
Every statistic and pooling op must use the row-4 mask, and padded columns must not enter ranks, means, max or medians.
Rows 2-3 are nuisance covariates only: partial them out or use them as split keys, never feed them as direct evidence.
Use no t-statistic or negative-binomial association scores. Prefer rank-based statistics.
known_failures: Rank partial correlation and tercile statistics can be unstable or NaN for triples with few contacts or heavy ties from zero-inflated counts. The min_contacts guard and eps terms must hold.
The DeepSets branch may overfit the 10 training tiles and take weight from the closed-form stats. Differences under 0.02 lr_auprc versus a stats-only variant are unresolved.
The 0.592 of the cited prior run cannot be verified (no code supplied), so exact reproduction may differ in feature normalisation or head details.
Smooth L1 on 0/1 labels at about 7% prevalence is weakly sensitive to rare positives and may bias the score toward the base rate. Ranking quality may be lower than with focal_cw.
suggested_directions: Run the baseline_config as is with 5-fold tile-grouped CV on TRAIN. Pick epochs by CV lr_auprc, then run the final fit and compare on validation.
Report a bootstrap that resamples the 7 validation tiles, not the 21 datasets. Treat differences under 0.02 as unresolved.
If the run constraint on output_type is lifted, swap loss_type to focal_cw with no other change. This is the first controlled comparison.
Then run the single-factor ablations listed above, one per trial.
expert_advice.rationale: The statistics are fixed, parameter-free and rank-based, so the model has little to overfit. The learned part only has to weight about six evidence channels and a small set embedding. This is the safest structure when there are only 10 training tiles and the target is a within-dataset ranking.

They are concatenated with a small masked DeepSets embedding and fed to a 2-layer MLP head. Named in the human directive with reported validation 0.592. Not yet tested in this project.

memo_consistency_notes: CONFLICT: the human directive asks for the built-in focal_cw loss and says not to use SmoothL1 on 0/1 labels. The run declares output_type must be 'regressor', and the output/loss rule allows only smooth_l1 for a regressor; a regressor with focal_cw would be rejected before training. Custom losses are unavailable and the directive also refuses them. The binding run constraint takes precedence, so loss_type is smooth_l1 despite the human instruction. This is a forced deviation, not a preference. The mitigation is that the model emits a sigmoid-bounded probability, so smooth_l1 acts as a Brier-like proper scoring rule on 0/1 labels instead of an unbounded regression. If the output_type restriction is lifted, switch to classifier + focal_cw with no architecture change. The memo and the human instruction both require focal_cw.

Task text says classification, but the run constraint allows only output_type 'regressor'. The model emits [B,1] in [0,1] (sigmoid of a logit), which also satisfies the [B,1] score contract. Only within-dataset ranking matters.

Memo specification followed: n_stats=6, embed_dim=16, hidden_dim=32, dropout=0.1, 2-layer MLP head. Additions beyond the memo are only implementation details (phi_hidden_dim, min_contacts guard, ridge_lambda, eps), and no new evidence channels were added.

The memo lists 'neighbour-count split' without a formula. It is implemented as the Spearman difference between high- and low-neighbour-count halves of the contact cells (split on the masked median of row 3). Row 3 is only a split key here. Other definitions are possible, so this is an interpretation.

Honest status: the 0.592 validation score of the prior lr_contact_contrast_gbm_head comes from the human directive only. It is not reproduced or verified in this project, and no source code was supplied. The design here is a re-implementation from the textual description, so the memo's 0.57 prediction is a prior-based guess.
The prior run name includes 'gbm', but the memo and human directive specify a 2-layer MLP head. The MLP is used and no gradient-boosting component is implemented.
